_comment: FRIC-total-accounting meta-gate policy (DATA, not code). Founder decision 2026-06-10: every friction-ledger row must terminate in a gate, an automation, or an explicit accepted-risk entry. This gate is the closed-loop accounting tracker for the friction ledger (Google SRE postmortem action-item model: every action item must have an owner and verifiable closure). ALL repo-specifics live here; the Rust engine is neutral and runs on any repo by repointing ledger_path + status_taxonomy. See ADR-0544.

product_contract.born_pack_shaped: Every repo-specific value (ledger path, the free-text status taxonomy, the required-field set, the evidence policy) is DATA here. The Rust kernel hardcodes no repo path nor any oyatie string; another repo adopts this gate by editing this policy.
product_contract.closed_loop: A friction is accounted iff it (a) is a schema-valid row, (b) declares a disposition (enforcement_fix), and (c) when in a terminal/accepted-risk class, cites its enforcement artifact via the evidence field. Mirrors Google SRE postmortem action-item closure.
product_contract.never_discourage_logging: Appending a friction row never fails the gate by itself. Only schema/disposition/closure-integrity violations on NEW rows block; legacy debt is baselined and may only shrink.
product_contract.execution: Buck2-native Rust gate; no Cargo command is required for enforcement.

purpose: FRIC-total-accounting meta-gate. Every friction-ledger row must terminate in a gate, an automation, or an explicit accepted-risk entry; unconverted/undisposed/unevidenced frictions block merges like code debt.
